overview.description: Encaje, also known as Mus Francés (French Mus), is a version of the Basque game Mus adapted for 3 or 5 players. Unlike standard Mus, Encaje is played without partnerships—each player competes individually. The unique twist is that there is no winner, only a loser; the goal is to avoid being the last player with stones remaining.

history.evolution: Encaje represents an adaptation of Mus to accommodate different player counts. The elimination of partnerships and the inverse objective (avoid losing rather than winning) creates a fundamentally different social dynamic compared to standard Mus.
history.cultural: The game reflects Basque card game culture, where betting and bluffing are highly valued skills. The tradition of the loser paying for drinks adds a social penalty that enhances the game's entertainment value.

setup.dealing:
Two methods available:
1. Standard deal: 4 cards to each player, with 'mus' round for exchanging cards
2. Alternative deal: 5 cards to each player, each discards 1 face down before betting
Deal rotates anticlockwise

rules.objective: Be the first player to get rid of all your stones. The last player with stones remaining is the loser.
rules.gameplay:
Four betting phases per hand: Grande (high cards), Chica (low cards), Pares (pairs), and Juego/Punto (card combinations).

1. Grande: Bet on having the highest cards
2. Chica: Bet on having the lowest cards
3. Pares: Bet on having pairs (only players with pairs participate)
4. Juego/Punto: Bet on card point totals (31 is best juego, punto is fallback)

Betting proceeds anticlockwise from the mano (player to dealer's right). Players can pass, bet (minimum 2), see, or raise (minimum increase of 2).
keyRules: Cannot bet more stones than you currently possess
Players with no stones cannot participate in betting
The loser is the last player with stones remaining
If only one player has pares or juego, they score without betting

strategy.basic: Learn the Mus hand rankings thoroughly. Understand when to say 'mus' for card exchange versus 'no hay mus' to begin betting. Manage your stone count carefully—don't risk too many stones on marginal hands.
strategy.intermediate: Observe opponent betting patterns to deduce hand strength. Bluff selectively in early phases to force opponents to fold. In the pares and juego phases, accurately assess whether your hand justifies seeing or raising.
strategy.advanced: Master the art of stone management. Sometimes it's better to fold and conserve stones than to risk elimination. Use position (being the mano) to control betting tempo. When low on stones, play more conservatively; when opponents are low, apply pressure.
tips: Don't bluff too frequently—observant opponents will catch on
Keep track of how many stones each player has
Consider folding early if your hand is weak across all phases
Remember that the goal is to lose stones, not win them
Pay attention to which cards have been played in previous hands

fold.description: Concede the current betting phase to avoid losing more stones.
fold.constraints: During betting phase after someone bets. Cannot win the phase.

bet.description: Propose to stake stones on the outcome of the current betting phase.
bet.constraints: Minimum bet is 2 stones; maximum is number of stones you currently have. Cannot bet more than available stones.

raise.description: Increase the bet after another player has bet.
raise.constraints: Each raise must increase the stake by at least 2 stones. Cannot raise more than your available stones.

declare.description: Declare if you have pares or juego in the corresponding betting phase.
declare.constraints: Before pares phase: announce if you have pares. Before juego phase: announce if you have juego. Players without stones cannot declare.

award_pot.reason: No pot; winner determined by game rules.

play_card.reason: Vying game with betting; cards compared in showdown, not played to table.

pass.description: Pass without betting in the current betting phase.
pass.constraints: At the start of a betting phase, if you don't want to bet, you can pass to allow the next player to act.

engine.handRankingSystem: Grande: Three of a kind beats pairs beats high cards. Chica: Low hands ranked by lowest card. Pares: Pairs and two-pairs scored. Juego: Best combinations using all four cards to reach 31 (natural juego).
engine.deckDescription: Standard 40-card deck: forty cards in four French suits, with ranks Ace, 2 through 7, 10, Jack, Queen, and King (eights and nines removed); no jokers used in this Spanish betting game.
engine.suitDescription: French suit set: four suits—Spades, Hearts, Diamonds, and Clubs—each with ten cards (Ace, 2-7, 10, Jack, Queen, King) in this stripped forty-card deck.
engine.rankDescription: Stripped forty rank set: Ace, 2 through 7, 10, Jack, Queen, and King (eights and nines omitted), giving ten cards per suit for Encaje.

synthesis.shortDescription: Encaje, also known as Mus Francés (French Mus), is a Spanish vying game for 3-5 players adapted from Mus where each player competes individually with no partnerships. The unique objective is to eliminate all your stones—the last player with stones remaining is the loser.

scoring.description: Players start with 15-21 stones each and try to eliminate them through betting phases. Stones are removed from play based on showdown results and betting outcomes.
scoring.winCondition: The game ends when all players except one have eliminated all their stones and all temporary pots are settled. The last player remaining with stones is the loser of the game.
